gaps.explanation: 'Somewhere' is used in affirmative sentences; adjectives like 'quiet' follow the -where word.

gaps.sentence: There are trees on ___ side of the road.
gaps.hint: singular noun: each of the two sides
gaps.explanation: 'Either side' means each of the two sides; 'both' would need the plural 'sides'.

gaps.sentence: ___ time I visit Rome, I discover something new.
gaps.explanation: 'Every time I ...' introduces repeated occasions; 'all time' and 'whole time' are not used here.
'Far too much information' is the correct intensifier pattern; 'far much' and 'far very' do not exist.

gaps.sentence: We had very ___ rain this spring, so the garden suffered.
gaps.explanation: 'Little' means not much and is used with uncountables; the garden suffering shows an insufficient amount.

gaps.hint: general statement without 'the' — 'people' has no article
gaps.explanation: 'Most people' means people in general; 'most of' needs 'the' (most of the people).

gaps.sentence: This suitcase is ___ heavy to carry.
gaps.hint: adjective + this word + to-infinitive = impossible result
gaps.explanation: 'Too heavy to carry' means it is more heavy than possible; 'very' and 'so' cannot be followed directly by 'to'.

gaps.sentence: ___ the information you gave was correct.
gaps.explanation: 'All the information' is correct; 'none/neither' would need 'of' and 'both' requires two separate countable items.
